united-kingdom/london-westminster.name: Westminster, Buckingham Palace and the Thames
united-kingdom/london-westminster.description: Big Ben, Westminster Abbey, the palace and a walk along the river.
united-kingdom/london-westminster.details: Westminster has the Houses of Parliament, Westminster Abbey and Buckingham Palace with the guard change. A walk along the South Bank passes the London Eye, Tate Modern and Borough Market. Allow a full day, and book Abbey tickets online.

united-kingdom/london-museums-theatre.name: British Museum, National Gallery and a West End show
united-kingdom/london-museums-theatre.description: Free national museums and an evening of theatre.
united-kingdom/london-museums-theatre.details: The British Museum and National Gallery are free to enter. Seats for West End shows are cheaper at the TKTS booth on the day. Book popular shows ahead. Covent Garden and Soho are close for pre-theatre dinner.

united-kingdom/london-tower-greenwich.name: Tower of London, Tower Bridge and Greenwich
united-kingdom/london-tower-greenwich.description: The crown jewels and a river trip to the home of Greenwich Mean Time.
united-kingdom/london-tower-greenwich.details: The Tower of London holds the Crown Jewels and Yeoman Warder tours. Walk across Tower Bridge, then take a river boat to Greenwich for the Maritime Museum, the Royal Observatory and the Cutty Sark. Book Tower tickets in advance.

united-kingdom/windsor-oxford.name: Windsor Castle or Oxford colleges
united-kingdom/windsor-oxford.description: A royal castle and the dreaming spires of a university city, each an hour from London.
united-kingdom/windsor-oxford.details: Windsor Castle is the oldest inhabited castle in the world, with State Apartments. Oxford has historic colleges, the Bodleian Library and Christ Church, which inspired the Harry Potter films. Both are easy by train from London.

united-kingdom/stonehenge.name: Stonehenge and Salisbury
united-kingdom/stonehenge.description: The prehistoric stone circle on Salisbury Plain and a cathedral city.
united-kingdom/stonehenge.details: Stonehenge stands on open downland with a visitor centre and audio guide. Entry needs a timed ticket booked ahead. Salisbury has a cathedral with the oldest working clock in England and a Magna Carta copy. Combine with Bath on a day trip.

united-kingdom/bath-roman-baths.name: Bath Roman Baths and the Royal Crescent
united-kingdom/bath-roman-baths.description: A Georgian spa city built on Roman hot springs.
united-kingdom/bath-roman-baths.details: The Roman Baths are a well-preserved temple and bathing complex, and Bath Abbey, the Royal Crescent and Pulteney Bridge are close. Thermae Bath Spa has a rooftop pool. Book Roman Baths tickets online, and go early or late to avoid crowds.

united-kingdom/cotswolds-villages.name: Cotswolds villages
united-kingdom/cotswolds-villages.description: Honey-coloured stone villages such as Bourton-on-the-Water, Bibury and Chipping Campden.
united-kingdom/cotswolds-villages.details: The Cotswolds are best by car or on a small-group tour. Villages such as Bibury, Castle Combe and Broadway have stone cottages, tea rooms and pubs. Walks follow the Cotswold Way. Visit early to avoid day-trippers.

united-kingdom/york-minster-shambles.name: York Minster, city walls and the Shambles
united-kingdom/york-minster-shambles.description: A medieval walled city with Britain largest Gothic cathedral and a crooked old lane.
united-kingdom/york-minster-shambles.details: York Minster has a Great East Window and a tower climb. The city walls can be walked for 3.4 kilometres, and the Shambles is the narrow street of overhanging medieval houses. The Jorvik Viking Centre and the National Railway Museum are family favourites.

united-kingdom/lake-district-windermere.name: Lake District: Windermere cruise and fell walk
united-kingdom/lake-district-windermere.description: England largest lake, steamers, and short mountain hikes with views.
united-kingdom/lake-district-windermere.details: Windermere has cruises from Bowness and Ambleside, and nearby fells such as Orrest Head offer easy hikes with views. Beatrix Potter and Wordsworth sites are close. Weather is changeable and often wet, so carry waterproofs.

united-kingdom/belfast-titanic.name: Belfast Titanic Quarter and murals
united-kingdom/belfast-titanic.description: The shipyard where the Titanic was built and political murals on the Falls Road.
united-kingdom/belfast-titanic.details: Titanic Belfast is a museum on the slipway of the famous ship, and the city has Black Taxi tours of the murals, St George Market and the Cathedral Quarter. A good introduction to the Troubles and the peace process. Allow a full day.

united-kingdom/giants-causeway.name: Giant Causeway and the Antrim coast
united-kingdom/giants-causeway.description: Basalt columns on the coast, rope bridges and Dunluce Castle.
united-kingdom/giants-causeway.details: The Giant Causeway is a UNESCO site of around 40,000 hexagonal basalt columns. The Carrick-a-Rede rope bridge, Dunluce Castle and the Dark Hedges are other stops on a coastal day trip from Belfast. Book bridge tickets ahead.
